principles: Reaction functions are bank-specific; no universal macro-to-rates-to-FX rule is assumed.
Rates are an observed repricing layer, not a binary confirmation gate.
Convergence and divergence are preserved as information states, not automatically promoted to trading rules.
Only PIT-safe or explicitly conservative historical inputs may enter historical diagnostics.
Unsupported historical blocks remain WITHHELD and contribute no vote.
No threshold tuning, ex-post weighting, window selection, or engine changes are allowed from these diagnostics.
Any vNext candidate must beat the frozen baseline through chronological OOS evidence before promotion.

FED_USD.evidence_summary: A proper Fed-vs-ECB reaction-function comparison is not yet admissible because USD Labour PIT is withheld. No revised fallback should be used.
next_priority: Unlock USD Labour first-release PIT from a genuinely archival source.
Certify a coherent US 2Y/front-end historical series for observed repricing.
Then run Fed-specific state replay using labour + inflation as co-primary inputs.

tests_completed: EUR wages plus 5-market-day EUR2Y alignment diagnostic

key_evidence.walkforward_interpretation: 20d signal remained positive but weakened OOS; not statistically locked. Historical wage availability dates are conservative checkpoints, so the test measures post-checkpoint alignment, not clean release causality.

ECB_EUR.evidence_summary: ECB shows the most encouraging evidence that policy-relevant wage pressure and front-end repricing jointly improve interpretation, especially around 20d, but sample size and timestamp quality are insufficient for engine promotion.
next_priority: Improve exact historical wage release timestamps where possible.
Extend services-inflation PIT before 2024 if official first-published vintages can be certified.
Re-run on the exact same base event cohort before any future comparison or model promotion.

key_evidence.ois_filter_result: Simple 5-day same-direction 2Y OIS confirmation did not add robust value OOS and should not be used as a mechanical GBP filter.
key_evidence.labour_replay_note: Frozen Labour showed possible slower 60d persistence in a separate descriptive replay, but not enough evidence for promotion.

BOE_GBP.evidence_summary: BoE evidence rejects a mechanical 'labour + wages + services + 2Y confirmation = GBP' rule. Policy-relevant domestic pressure matters conceptually, but expected policy path, inflation level vs target, growth trade-off, MPC regime and surprise-vs-consensus likely matter materially.
next_priority: Do not add more ad-hoc GBP combinations.
Future BoE research should add predeclared policy-regime context or consensus-surprise data only if PIT-safe.
Keep wages/services/labour/OIS as separate dashboard evidence layers, not one score.

tests_completed: CAD Reaction Function State Replay Labour-only

key_evidence.core_headline_both_aligned_pooled_oos_in: Pooled OOS weakened materially to roughly 57% hit with near-flat positive mean, so the state is descriptive but not a locked edge.
key_evidence.rates_filter_result: Simple 5-day 2Y same-direction confirmation failed; divergent states can carry information and must not be discarded mechanically.
key_evidence.mixed_neutral_result: Mixed/neutral inflation-macro states were generally weaker, especially around 20d, supporting state classification as an explanatory layer.

BOC_CAD.evidence_summary: CAD is the strongest current proof-of-concept for the vNext architecture: combining Growth, Labour and persistent inflation state improves descriptive coherence, while headline and rates add context. However, OOS weakening prevents promotion to a mechanical engine rule.
next_priority: Stop searching new CAD combinations to avoid overfitting.
Use CAD as the reference implementation for dashboard Reaction State presentation.
Revisit only with genuinely new OOS data or a predeclared additional PIT-safe layer.

RBA_AUD.evidence_summary: Live data are certified, but historical PIT blocks required for a reaction-function replay are not yet available.
next_priority: Certify historical first-release labour and inflation archives.
Certify a coherent AUD front-end/OIS history.
Then test a dual-mandate state replay with predeclared architecture.

RBNZ_NZD.evidence_summary: NZD cannot yet support a professional historical reaction-function replay without fabricating missing PIT layers.
next_priority: Build historical first-release inflation PIT first.
Then add labour/growth only as secondary layers according to remit regime.
Do not use synthetic OIS or revised-history fallback.

SNB_CHF.evidence_summary: A CHF reaction function must explicitly preserve FX conditions as a policy variable; labour should not be treated as a direct Fed-style input. Historical PIT remains incomplete.
next_priority: Certify historical inflation PIT.
Design a predeclared FX-monetary-conditions layer before testing.
Add front-end rates only as observed repricing, not as a confirmation gate.

BOJ_JPY.evidence_summary: Historical JPY Labour reconstruction is structurally feasible, but activation is false because archived releases do not yet provide a certified intraday/event-time policy. BoJ should be modelled through wage-price-cycle persistence, not labour alone.
next_priority: Resolve official release-calendar/event-time policy for Labour PIT activation.
Certify historical wages and inflation PIT.
Only then build a BoJ wage-price-cycle reaction replay.

cross_country_conclusions: No universal rates-confirmation filter survived the current tests.
CAD supports the explanatory value of bank-specific macro state decomposition but not a locked trading rule.
GBP demonstrates that even economically sensible policy inputs do not map mechanically into FX returns.
EUR remains promising but constrained by conservative wage timestamps and limited services-history length.
The dashboard should expose separate layers: data importance -> central-bank interpretation -> market repricing -> FX price response.
The next research priority should be determined by data readiness, not by searching for the best historical return pattern.
research_priority_order: USD/Fed: unlock Labour PIT and coherent US front-end history
EUR/ECB: improve timestamp quality and extend services PIT
JPY/BoJ: activate labour event-time and add wages/inflation PIT
CHF/SNB: inflation plus FX-conditions PIT architecture
CAD/BoC: hold architecture fixed; wait for new OOS evidence
GBP/BoE: hold current evidence; no further ad-hoc combinations
